problem: Open-world mobile manipulation needs global scene understanding plus state tracking, but semantic-map/CLIP-feature pipelines struggle with compositional instructions and need dense 3D reconstruction, while off-the-shelf VLMs (GPT-4o) hallucinate and fail at egocentric decision-making and grounding due to domain shift.
motivation: Generalist home robots must follow open-ended instructions in unseen environments, and VLMs offer generalization and reasoning that embedding-based retrieval lacks. Precise geometry is only needed locally, and can be recovered by 2D-to-3D projection when the robot approaches the target, so a VLM with multi-view posed frames and self-tracked history could drive planners directly. Generic VLMs suffer from rare grounding tasks, state tracking, and embodiment priors, motivating simulation-synthesized instruction tuning.
key_idea: Fine-tune a single multi-image VLM (OWMM-VLM) on simulation-synthesized agentic episodes so it retrieves posed frames, tracks its own state via textual history, and outputs function-call actions with bbox coordinates that feed navigation and motion planners.
insight: Fine-tuning on synthetic data massively closes the gap to GPT-4o (ego-centric decision-making 97.85% vs 48.53%; image retrieval 87.54% vs 46.46%), and specialized grounding models (RoboPoint/PIVOT) don't fix the decision-making failures. Ablations show that bbox output (vs raw points) leverages pretrained grounding priors (object grounding 0.93→0.65 when using coordinates) and that reasoning+summarization matter (retrieval 79.04→65.86). Data volume matters (log-like scaling) while scene/object diversity has little effect (within ~5%).
method: Agent framework: the VLM takes instruction, pre-mapped posed RGB frames (pose graph), the current egocentric frame, and its own history, and outputs a high-level action plus updated history each step.

Action space: four function-call actions (posed image retrieval, navigate to point, pick, place) with bounding-box coordinates; the box center is back-projected with depth to 3D and executed by a path planner, an OMPL-style motion planner, and a gripper controller.

OWMM-VLM: InternVL-2.5 (8B: InternViT-300M+InternLM2.5-7B; 38B: InternViT-6B+Qwen2.5) fine-tuned with ViT frozen and MLP+LLM trainable, generating JSON with chain-of-thought reasoning, context summary and action.

Agentic data synthesis: PDDL task sequences executed in Habitat (HSSD 143 scenes, YCB+GSO objects, Fetch robot); key steps are selected and filtered for visibility/reachability, with images re-rendered afterwards; reasoning/summary from templates paraphrased by GPT-4o-mini; receptacle labels rewritten by GPT-4o.

Dataset: 21,046 valid episodes, ~235k annotations (pick 64.7K, place 68.9K, nav 59.6K, search-frame 378.8K multi-image pairs); the training/test split uses 113:30 scenes and 137:20 objects, giving 152k train and 4k test entries.
Real-world deployment: Robi Butler Fetch system with SLAM pre-mapping; actions are visualized and require human confirmation before execution.

setting.training_data: 152k simulation-synthesized instruction-tuning entries from Habitat HSSD (143 scenes, 157 objects, 21k episodes), 1 epoch
setting.observation: posed multi-view RGB pre-mapping frames + egocentric head RGB (+depth for back-projection) + text history
setting.action_space: high-level function calls (image retrieval, nav-to-point, pick, place) with bbox coordinates, executed by path/motion planners
setting.simulator: Habitat 3.0 (HomeRobot framework, HSSD scenes, Fetch robot)
setting.privileged: pre-mapping phase: pose graph with posed RGB images and 2D occupancy map assumed available; no other GT at test

results: OWMM-VLM-38B reaches 97.85% egocentric decision accuracy and 87.54% image retrieval versus GPT-4o's 48.53% and 46.46%, and 21.90% full-task success (51.52% lenient) versus 0.33% (1.68%) for GPT-4o+PIVOT and 0.33% (3.03%) for GPT-4o+RoboPoint, which have dead loops in ~60% of episodes. In real-world single-step tests the sim-only-trained model gets 90% total accuracy versus 46.67% for the GPT-4o+PIVOT/RoboPoint baselines.
limitations: Assumes a pre-mapping phase with posed frames and a 2D occupancy map; absolute full-task success is still low (21.9% strict), with goal-image retrieval a bottleneck (30.39%).
Limited to suction-style pick/place and does not handle dexterous end effectors; embodiment priors (arm reach) are tied to Fetch, so cross-embodiment transfer may fail.
Real-world evaluation is only 10 single-step samples with human confirmation, not autonomous full-episode runs.
